title: TrumpFile claims a 2008 New York Times Epstein profile was arranged by Howard Rubenstein
description_short: TrumpFile claims a 2008 New York Times Epstein profile was arranged by Howard Rubenstein
description_medium: TrumpFile’s timeline page states that The New York Times published a flattering article about Jeffrey Epstein on January 3, 2008, and claims publicist Howard Rubenstein arranged the interview. It says his clients included Donald Trump and Jared Kushner. The page does not provide the NYT article or a supporting source link; the claimed client overlap does not establish Trump or Kushner influenced the coverage.
description_long: TrumpFile’s timeline page describes a purported New York Times article about Jeffrey Epstein as flattering and says publicist Howard Rubenstein arranged the interview. The page’s title assigns the item a January 3, 2008 date, and its text says Rubenstein’s client list also included the Trump and Kushner families, Rupert Murdoch, and Adnan Khashoggi. These are claims made by the supplied TrumpFile page, not independently established facts about the article or its preparation. The extracted page provides no link to the New York Times story or to evidence for the arrangement; it says source links would be added later. A client relationship, even if accurate, does not show that Trump or Kushner requested, shaped, or approved the coverage. The underlying article’s publication date, text, tone, and Rubenstein’s role remain unconfirmed. This internal draft preserves the page’s specific claim while identifying its limits. It removes the unrelated national-security and war tags and does not state that Trump influenced the article. Keep the entry publication-ineligible until the original article and claim-level documentation can be reviewed.

title: Supplied allegation: Trump administration adopted a blanket policy resisting congressional oversight in 2025
description_short: The supplied record alleges a blanket 2025 Trump administration policy resisting congressional subpoenas and oversight.
description_medium: An unverified supplied account alleges that, beginning January 20, 2025, the Trump administration refused congressional subpoenas and oversight requests as a blanket policy. It also alleges officials were told not to testify, documents were withheld across agencies, inspectors general needed White House clearance before reporting to Congress, and the administration delayed court orders. The supplied material does not substantiate these claims or identify an order, subpoena, agency, case, or supporting source.
description_long: The supplied account alleges that, beginning January 20, 2025, the second Trump administration followed a blanket policy of rejecting congressional subpoenas and oversight requests. It further alleges the administration asserted unusually broad executive-privilege claims, instructed officials not to testify before committees, withheld documents across agencies, and required inspectors general to obtain White House clearance before reporting findings to Congress. The original text also says courts ordered compliance and that the administration delayed and appealed those rulings, but it names no court, case, subpoena, agency, official, or decision. Its description of the policy as unprecedented and as dismantling a constitutional check is likewise an allegation, not a finding established by the supplied materials. The packet contains no directive, correspondence, court ruling, or claim-level source that confirms these details or shows that they applied across the administration. This internal draft preserves the alleged scope while keeping each element clearly attributed and unverified. It does not state that a blanket policy, unlawful refusal, court order, or universal inspector-general rule existed. Keep it publication-ineligible unless specific, dated oversight disputes and primary documentation support a narrower account.
date_precision: supplied claim start date; not independently verified

title: Trump promoted a $59.99 branded Bible; $300 million in revenue is unsupported
description_short: Trump promoted the $59.99 God Bless the USA Bible; AP reporting does not substantiate the $300 million revenue claim.
description_medium: On March 26, 2024, Trump promoted the God Bless the USA Bible and urged supporters to buy it from a website listing the price at $59.99. AP later reported close to 120,000 copies shipped to the United States from China by late March and estimated about $7 million in potential retail sales at the minimum price. AP also cited a disclosure showing $300,000 in CIC Ventures Bible royalties, while noting the period and any additional payments were unclear. The $300 million revenue claim is unsupported by these reports.
description_long:
On March 26, 2024, Donald Trump promoted the “God Bless the USA Bible,” urging supporters to buy it from a website listing the price at $59.99. The website said Trump’s name and image were used under a paid license from CIC Ventures, a company he reported owning. The book combined a King James Version Bible with U.S. founding documents and the Pledge of Allegiance.

The original title’s $300 million revenue figure is not substantiated by the reporting reviewed here. In October 2024, the Associated Press reported that trade records showed close to 120,000 copies shipped from China to the United States between early February and late March. At the minimum retail price, AP estimated potential sales revenue for those shipments at about $7 million. AP also cited a financial disclosure showing $300,000 in Bible royalties earned by CIC Ventures, while stating that the disclosure period and any additional payments were unclear. Shipment estimates, potential retail sales, company royalties, and Trump’s total receipts are different measures; these reports do not establish total eventual sales or payments. The corrected entry records the promotion and licensing arrangement, removes the unsupported $300 million claim, and leaves final revenue and total royalties unknown.

title: Supplied allegation: FISA surveillance monitored journalists’ government sources in March 2025
description_short: The supplied record alleges March 2025 FISA surveillance of journalists’ communications with government sources.
description_medium: An unverified supplied account alleges that the Trump administration used FISA warrants in March 2025 to monitor communications between national-security journalists and government sources. It further alleges that surveillance was intended to identify reporters’ sources and could expose journalists to prosecution. No warrant, court order, named reporter, case docket, or corroborating report appears in the supplied record, so the surveillance, attribution to the administration, and claimed prosecutorial risk remain unverified.
description_long: The supplied account alleges that in March 2025 the Trump administration used FISA warrants to monitor communications between national-security journalists and government officials who served as sources. It describes the alleged activity as Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court-authorized monitoring intended to expose newsgathering contacts, and says the resulting information could be used to identify or prosecute reporters. These statements are allegations in the packet, not findings. The record names no journalist, source, warrant, docket number, agency, application, or FISC order, and provides no reporting that independently corroborates the alleged program. The public Office of the Director of National Intelligence release retrieved during research concerns a March 2025 Section 702 renewal opinion and related procedures; it does not establish the journalist-surveillance claim or identify a warrant targeting reporters. Its public summary also does not resolve what may appear in classified materials. The supplied record does not establish that any reporter was monitored, a confidential source was identified, or anyone faced prosecution. Retain the date only as the packet’s proposed timing and preserve the allegation as unverified. Do not present surveillance or prosecutorial risk as established fact.
date_precision: supplied date; day is provisional and not independently verified
organization_tags: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

impact_proposal.basis: Supplied allegation only; ODNI’s public March 2025 FISC release does not substantiate journalist targeting.
impact_proposal.notes: Defer pending a claim-level source. Do not infer harm or reach from the seriousness of the allegation.
